site.arxiv.org "How Much Knowledge Can You Pack"

sources_considered.why: Primary experiments report improved few-shot performance in GPT-3.
Primary experiments demonstrate retained factual information and discuss hallucination in the same models.
Its conditional mathematical explanation is relevant background, but an alternative explanation alone would not disprove a contribution from consciousness.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Tom B. Brown and colleagues
evidence_items.explanation: The experiments demonstrate usable abilities acquired through training and adaptation to examples. They contradict an absolute absence of learning under the operational reading, without establishing consciousness.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Adam Roberts, Colin Raffel and Noam Shazeer
evidence_items.explanation: The study tests question answering using information retained in model parameters and also observes hallucination. This directly undermines the premise that hallucinating models have no usable learned information.

unresolved_gaps: These experiments do not measure subjective consciousness or resolve philosophical definitions of knowledge.
They do not provide a complete causal account of every hallucination.
